title_en: How Do You Read This in Chinese

sentences.en: My friend and I were eating at a restaurant, and the waiter gave us a menu.
While I was looking at the menu, I saw a character I didn't recognize, and didn't know how to read it either.
I asked my friend: "How do you read this character?"
My friend said: "This character is read xiā — shrimp. Shrimp is delicious."
I read it once, then read it again, and finally I could read it.
The waiter asked us what dish we wanted to order, and I said right away: "I want shrimp."
When the waiter brought the shrimp, I looked at the menu and read it once more: "Shrimp!"

quiz.q: What does the narrator ask about the unfamiliar character?
What food does the character turn out to name?
What does the narrator do when the shrimp arrives?

grammar.p: 这个字怎么读？(How do you read this character?)
grammar.e: 怎么 + verb asks how to do something — here it asks how an unfamiliar character is pronounced.
grammar.x: 这个字怎么读？— How do you read this character?

grammar.p: 又 + verb（again, for a repeated action）
grammar.e: 又 marks that an action happens again; here it shows the narrator practicing the reading a second time.
grammar.x: 我念了一遍，又念了一遍，终于会读了。— I read it once, then again, and finally could read it.

grammar.e: 把 moves the object in front of the verb to focus on what happens to it — here, the waiter brings the shrimp.
grammar.x: 服务员把虾拿来的时候，我看着菜单，又念了一次：“虾！”— When the waiter brought the shrimp, I looked at the menu and read it once more: “Shrimp!”
